paper.title: CarMem: Enhancing Long-Term Memory in LLM Voice Assistants through Category-Bounding

latest_version.version_label: COLING 2025 Industry Track camera-ready, reviewed on 2026-08-31

evidence.paraphrase: CarMem is a public synthetic multi-turn, multi-session in-car assistant dataset built from 100 user profiles. It contains 1,000 preference-extraction conversations, 1,000 later retrieval utterances and 3,000 maintenance utterances, with ground-truth preferences and maintenance actions.

The benchmark separately measures category-bound preference extraction, opt-out behavior, maintenance decisions for equal, negated and different preferences, and semantic retrieval of the correct stored preference. Its labels expose redundant-memory handling and contradiction updates rather than only final response quality.

adjudication_notes: Included as memory_adjacent because it is an explicitly named, public long-term-memory dataset used in the manuscript Table 1, but its examples are text conversations in a voice-assistant application setting rather than recorded speech.

primary_modality follows the manuscript's Audio and speech memory grouping and the in-car voice-assistant deployment domain. The record must not be interpreted as evidence that CarMem evaluates speaker identity, prosody or other acoustic-memory capabilities.

2026-09-17 scope review: A synthetic text-conversation protocol directly measures preference extraction, retrieval and maintenance. Voice-assistant motivation does not make the evaluated inputs acoustic. Retained and explicitly labeled as a text-only comparison; it is not evidence of multimodal-memory performance. The legacy scope_status field is not a Table 2 exclusion rule.
